goals: Mechanistic: quantify how water partitioning (ET, surface runoff, sub-surface drainage/recharge, snowmelt timing) varies with elevation-driven forcing and soil texture across the Naches HUC8
Validation: compare simulated states/fluxes to in-domain observations — BLOCKED, no observations provided in the brief
key_processes: surface runoff vs sub-surface drainage partitioning

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM resolves 1-D water/energy partitioning and snow; spatial sampling spans the basin's elevation and soil heterogeneity. NLDAS-2 gives elevation-varying forcing across the 1625 m relief.

answerable: Soil-texture control on partitioning (SSURGO per-column lever)
Elevation control on partitioning via orographic NLDAS-2 precip/temperature and simulated snow/SWE (resolved to ~12 km)
Snowmelt-timing and SWE gradients with elevation (H2OSNO, QSNOMELT in default output), with expected ridgetop SWE underestimation

not_answerable.aspect: Sub-12 km terrain control (ridgeline vs narrow-valley forcing contrasts within one NLDAS cell)
not_answerable.why: NLDAS-2 has no within-cell lapse rate; sub-12 km terrain is unresolved

not_answerable.aspect: Any observation validation (SWE, streamflow, water table)
not_answerable.why: brief lists no in-domain observations; single-column stack also has no routing for gage comparison
cold-start columns begin at default ~8.8 m water table with recharge ~0; slow states are init artifacts without spin-up
not_answerable.needs: model spin-up or WTD-informed warm start

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation bands x dominant soil classes)
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 5 elevation bands capture the orographic forcing + rain-snow transition gradient across 1625 m relief; crossing with ~2-3 dominant SSURGO textures per band (as they occur) gives ~15 cells, plus light replication in the rain-snow transition and valley bottoms where partitioning is most sensitive -> ~20, matching the requested budget while remaining stratified rather than a blind grid.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Oversample the rain-snow transition band (~1000-1350 m) where melt-timing and runoff/recharge partitioning are most sensitive, and valley bottoms/riparian corridors where soil-moisture and drainage signals concentrate; span the actual soil textures present in each band rather than forcing absent classes.
sampling_strategy.replication: 1-2 extra columns in the rain-snow transition and valley band to sample soil variability where partitioning gradients are steepest

sampling_plan.reason: Warm, low-snow baseline; isolates soil-texture control on ET/runoff and captures riparian drainage where storage signals concentrate.
Transitional climate band; spans dominant textures to separate soil vs elevation forcing effects.
Most sensitive band for melt-timing and runoff/recharge partitioning; oversampled across textures to resolve the steepest gradient.
Snowmelt-dominated recharge regime; tests soil control under a snow-driven water input signal.
Peak-SWE and cold end-member of the elevation gradient (expect ridgetop SWE underestimation from 12 km forcing).

validation_design.comparison: none possible in-domain; flagged as gap — would be co-located to any SNOTEL station if ingested
validation_design.metric: bias/RMSE on peak SWE and melt-out date

validation_design.comparison: none possible — also requires routing/aggregation the single-column stack lacks

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline NLDAS-2 forcing (nearest 12 km cell), native SSURGO soil per column, with spin-up or WTD-informed warm start required if recharge/water-table targeted

requires_capabilities.why: NLDAS-2 has no within-cell lapse rate
requires_capabilities.blocks: resolving ridgeline vs narrow-valley forcing contrasts inside a single 12 km cell

requires_capabilities.capability: in-domain observation ingest (SNOTEL SWE, USGS streamflow)

requires_capabilities.why: single-column ELM has no lateral transport

requires_capabilities.capability: model spin-up or WTD-informed warm start
requires_capabilities.why: columns cold-start at default ~8.8 m water table with recharge ~0

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM + SSURGO raster sampling and HUC boundary resolver
requires_capabilities.why: expander must place stratified points from real terrain/soil
requires_capabilities.blocks: turning these rules into concrete coordinates

assumptions: User's request for 20 explicit coordinates + full configs is out of scope for design mode; delivered as a 20-column stratified STRATEGY the expander/configurator will realize.
Naches (CONUS) is covered by NLDAS-2 default forcing at 0.125 degrees.
Dominant soil textures per elevation band are as found by SSURGO sampling; absent classes are not forced.
Study is mechanistic-only given the empty observation lists; if recharge/water-table is a target, spin-up/warm-start is added.
open_questions: Are there SNOTEL or USGS gages in HUC 17030002 that could be ingested to enable validation?
Is the partitioning target restricted to fast fluxes (ET/runoff/snow) or does it include recharge/water table (which mandates spin-up)?
Confirm the forcing period of interest within 1980-2018 (affects NLDAS cost ~30 min/simulated year/column).
